help.place.desc: Drop, paste (Ctrl+Shift+V) or insert an image to float it over the panorama. Move, scale, rotate and flip it with the handles, choose Wrap or Persistent projection, then press Enter to merge.
help.shortcuts_intro: Every shortcut works in both the sphere and the flat view. On macOS, Ctrl is ⌘.
help.tip.1: Paint in the sphere view: what you draw is projected exactly onto the panorama, so lines stay straight in 360°.
help.tip.10: Placing a photo or logo? Use Persistent to keep it undistorted from one viewpoint, or Wrap to stick it onto the sphere. Hold Shift while dropping a 2:1 image to open it as a new panorama instead.
help.tip.2: The flat view shows the whole equirectangular image. Dimmed copies on each side show how the seam wraps around.
help.tip.3: Turn on the grid (G) to see the horizon and lines every 15° — the equator is highlighted.
help.tip.4: Keep the image at a 2:1 ratio (e.g. 4096 × 2048) so 360° viewers display it correctly.
help.tip.5: Export 360° JPG embeds GPano metadata, so Facebook, Google Photos and VR viewers open it as a panorama.
help.tip.6: Use “Rotate heading” to choose which direction the viewer faces when the panorama opens.
help.tip.7: Lock transparency on a layer to shade inside existing strokes without painting outside them.
help.tip.8: Projects (.pano) keep every layer, blend mode and opacity. Your work is backed up automatically.
help.tip.9: Custom brushes: import Photoshop .abr, GIMP .gbr/.gih or any PNG as a brush tip. Brushes are stamped on the sphere, so they look the same at the poles and across the seam.

place.mode.wrap.desc: Bends the image onto the sphere like a sticker: it keeps its size in degrees wherever you move it.
place.reaim.desc: Moves the projector to the current view direction, so the image faces you undistorted again.

tool.airbrush.desc: Very soft, low-flow spray that builds up color gradually.
tool.brush.desc: Soft round brush with smoothing — the everyday painting tool.
tool.custom.desc: Paints with any brush from your library — built-ins, Photoshop ABR, GIMP GBR/GIH or your own images — with spacing, angle, scatter and jitter.
tool.eraser.desc: Erases to transparency on the active layer. Uses its own size and softness.

tool.fill.desc: Fills a connected area with the primary color. The fill wraps around the 360° seam.
tool.pen.desc: Crisp, hard-edged lines. Great for line art and details.
